docs.title: StaffOps Grafana Plugins
docs.text: Monorepo of Grafana plugins (panels and apps) for the StaffOps platform. Each plugin is a self-contained package under packages/, versioned and signed independently. Every plugin is frontend-only (React + TypeScript) — there are no datasource plugins and no Go backends; plugins consume datasources that already exist or talk to other Grafana apps.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: Plugin Type What it does Service Map Panel panel A DAG service map built from Tempo service-graph metrics — health, animated traffic, cascade filtering, drill-down. AIgent Squad Chat app A conversational UI to AIgent Squad (SRE-agentic assistant) — streams answers through the Grafana LLM app.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text: Principle Consequence Frontend-only No Go backends; secrets and orchestration live in existing services (LLM app, datasources). One package per plugin Independent versioning, signing, and release per plugin. No speculative abstraction Shared libraries are created only when a second consumer needs them (rule of three). Docker-only builds No local SDKs required — Node 22 + pnpm run inside containers. Spec-driven Each feature has specs/<feature>/{requirements,design,tasks}.md before code.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The repository is a pnpm workspace monorepo. Each Grafana plugin is an independent package; shared tooling (build config, linting, TypeScript) is consistent across packages, but each plugin ships and versions on its own.

graph TD
    subgraph Monorepo
        WS["pnpm-workspace.yaml"] --> P1["staffops-servicemap-panel"]
        WS --> P2["staffops-aigent-squad-chat-app"]
        SPECS["specs"] -. spec-driven .-> P1
        SPECS -. spec-driven .-> P2
    end
    P1 -->|DataFrames| DS[("Prometheus / Tempo")]
    P2 -->|"grafana/llm"| LLM["Grafana LLM app"] --> SQUAD["AIgent Squad"]

docs.title: Plugin types in this repo
docs.text: Type Grafana surface Example Data source Panel A visualization added to dashboards staffops-servicemap-panel DataFrames from configured datasources App Custom nav pages / whole experiences staffops-aigent-squad-chat-app The Grafana LLM app (via @grafana/llm)

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
• No Go backend — every plugin is frontend-only. Anything needing a server-side secret (e.g. the AIgent Squad token) delegates to an existing app (the Grafana LLM app).
  • Immutable, signed releases — each plugin is built and signed per version.
  • Docker-only builds — reproducible via node:22 containers; no host SDKs.

docs.title: No local SDKs — Docker only
docs.text:
The repo builds through Node 22 + pnpm inside containers. No host SDKs are required.

# Build a single plugin (from repo root)
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app node:22-slim sh -c '
  corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9 --activate
  pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
  pnpm --filter <plugin-name> build
'

pnpm strict isolation + tslib

The scaffolded webpack config is compiled by ts-node, which needs tslib. Under pnpm's strict node_modules, point NODE_PATH at the hoisted tslib when invoking webpack directly:

export NODE_PATH=/app/node_modules/.pnpm/tslib@2.8.1/node_modules:/app/node_modules
./node_modules/.bin/webpack -c ./.config/webpack/webpack.config.ts --env production

docs.title: Workspace scripts
docs.text:
The root package.json runs scripts recursively across packages/*:

Script Purpose build Production bundle (dist/) with subresource integrity dev Watch-mode build test / test:ci Jest unit tests (test:ci adds --coverage) typecheck tsc --noEmit lint / lint:fix ESLint sign Sign the plugin for distribution

docs.title: Subresource Integrity (SRI)
docs.text:
Plugins are built with webpack-subresource-integrity, so module.js carries integrity hashes for its lazy chunks. Editing a built dist/*.js by hand breaks the hash and the browser refuses to load the chunk (ChunkLoadError). Always rebuild instead of patching bundles.

Chunk renumbering + browser cache

Adding/removing modules can renumber webpack's lazy chunks (e.g. 590.js → 152.js). Grafana is an SPA and caches module.js; after a rebuild, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) or open an incognito window to pick up the new chunk references.

docs.title: Coverage gate
docs.text: Unit tests enforce ≥90% line coverage (test:ci --coverage). New features ship with their tests in the same change.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: Each plugin follows the standard GitHub Actions lanes: build, test, sast, release, and docs (this site). The docs workflow validates mkdocs build --strict on PRs and deploys to GitHub Pages on push to main.

docs.title: Monorepo Layout
docs.text:
grafana-plugins/
├── AGENTS.md                 # canonical agent guide (read first)
├── CLAUDE.md                 # pointer → AGENTS.md
├── mkdocs.yml                # this documentation site
├── specs/                    # spec-driven docs (requirements/design/tasks) per feature
│   ├── monorepo-foundation/  # structural decision (monorepo) + rationale
│   ├── nodegraph-servicemap/ # service map panel spec
│   └── aigent-squad-chat/    # AIgent Squad chat app spec
├── packages/                 # one directory per plugin
│   ├── staffops-servicemap-panel/
│   └── staffops-aigent-squad-chat-app/
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml        # workspace = packages/*
└── package.json              # recursive scripts (build/test/lint)

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• packages/ — one directory per plugin. A shared library (e.g. packages/graph-core) is created only when a second consumer actually needs it — no speculative abstraction (rule of three).
  • specs/ — spec-driven workflow. Every feature gets requirements.md, design.md, and tasks.md before implementation. Specs are neutral and versioned.
  • Naming — plugin IDs follow staffops-<name>-<type> (e.g. staffops-servicemap-panel, staffops-aigent-squad-chat-app), matching Grafana's orgName-pluginName-pluginType convention.

docs.title: Per-plugin package layout
docs.text:
packages/<plugin>/
├── src/
│   ├── plugin.json           # Grafana plugin manifest (id, type, dependencies)
│   ├── module.tsx            # plugin entry point (panel or AppPlugin)
│   └── components/ …         # React components
├── .config/                  # scaffolded webpack/jest/ts config (do not edit directly)
├── provisioning/             # local Grafana provisioning (datasources, apps, dashboards)
├── README.md                 # plugin-specific documentation
├── package.json              # scripts: build / dev / test / test:ci / typecheck / lint / sign
└── tsconfig.json

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Everything runs through Docker — no local Node/pnpm required. See the pages below.

  • Building & Testing — Docker build commands, workspace scripts, coverage
  • Creating a Plugin — scaffold a new panel or app plugin

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
# Build one plugin (from repo root)
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app node:22-slim sh -c '
  corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9 --activate
  pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
  pnpm --filter <plugin-name> test:ci   # tests + coverage
  pnpm --filter <plugin-name> build     # production bundle
'

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Spec-first — add specs/<feature>/{requirements,design,tasks}.md before code.
  • Tests ship with code — ≥90% line coverage, enforced in CI.
  • In-code docs in English; standalone docs may follow the repo/user language.
  • No new dependency when an existing one solves the problem.

docs.title: Building & Testing
docs.text: All commands run inside a node:22 container — the host needs no Node/pnpm.

docs.title: Install + build
docs.text:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app node:22-slim sh -c '
  corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9 --activate
  pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
  pnpm --filter <plugin-name> build
'

docs.title: Test with coverage
docs.text:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app/packages/<plugin> node:22-slim sh -c '
  export NODE_PATH=/app/node_modules/.pnpm/tslib@2.8.1/node_modules:/app/node_modules
  export PATH=./node_modules/.bin:$PATH
  jest --coverage
'

The coverage gate is ≥90% lines. Tests live next to the code (*.test.ts[x]).

docs.title: Direct webpack build (bypassing pnpm filter)
docs.text:
Useful when iterating on one plugin. The scaffolded config is compiled by ts-node, which needs tslib on NODE_PATH under pnpm's strict isolation:

docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app/packages/<plugin> node:22-slim sh -c '
  export NODE_PATH=/app/node_modules/.pnpm/tslib@2.8.1/node_modules:/app/node_modules
  export PATH=./node_modules/.bin:$PATH
  webpack -c ./.config/webpack/webpack.config.ts --env production
'

docs.title: Run a local Grafana with the plugin
docs.text:
Each plugin ships a compose file that mounts its dist/ into a Grafana container:

cd packages/<plugin>
docker compose up -d          # or docker-compose.e2e.yaml for the chat app
# open http://localhost:3000

Hard refresh after rebuild

Grafana is an SPA and caches module.js. After rebuilding, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) or use an incognito window, or the browser may load stale/renumbered chunks and fail with ChunkLoadError.

docs.title: Common pitfalls
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Cannot find module 'tslib' pnpm strict isolation Set NODE_PATH as above ChunkLoadError in the browser Stale cached module.js after rebuild Hard refresh / incognito Bundle edited by hand won't load Broken subresource-integrity hash Rebuild; never patch dist/*.js ERR_PNPM_NO_LOCKFILE Building without the workspace lockfile Install from repo root, or --no-frozen-lockfile

docs.title: Creating a Plugin
docs.text: New plugins are scaffolded with Grafana's create-plugin and reconciled to the monorepo conventions.

docs.title: 1. Write the spec first
docs.text:
specs/<feature>/
├── requirements.md   # user stories + acceptance criteria
├── design.md         # architecture, decisions, rationale, invariants
└── tasks.md          # discrete, trackable tasks

Spec-driven is a repo convention — freeze the design (and its rationale) before code.

docs.title: 2. Scaffold
docs.text:
# panel plugin
npx @grafana/create-plugin@latest --plugin-type=panel --org-name=staffops
# app plugin
npx @grafana/create-plugin@latest --plugin-type=app --org-name=staffops

Place the result in packages/staffops-<name>-<type>/. The plugin ID becomes staffops-<name>-<type> (e.g. staffops-servicemap-panel, staffops-aigent-squad-chat-app).

docs.title: 3. Reconcile to monorepo conventions
docs.text:
• License → MIT/Apache to match the repo.
  • Drop the packageManager pin (the workspace manages pnpm).
  • Ensure the package participates in the workspace (packages/*).
  • If the plugin depends on another Grafana app (e.g. the LLM app), declare it in plugin.json:
"dependencies": {
  "grafanaDependency": ">=12.3.0",
  "plugins": [{ "id": "grafana-llm-app", "type": "app", "name": "Grafana LLM" }]
}

docs.title: 4. Implement + test
docs.text:
• Keep it frontend-only — no Go backend. Delegate secrets/orchestration to existing apps (e.g. the Grafana LLM app).
  • Ship tests with the code (≥90% line coverage). Prefer testing the contract (public API / behaviour), not the implementation.

docs.title: 5. Config page (app plugins)
docs.text:
Expose behaviour knobs via AppPlugin.addConfigPage() — persisted in the plugin's jsonData. Never put secrets there; those belong in the datasource/app that owns them.

export const plugin = new AppPlugin<AppConfigJsonData>()
  .setRootPage(App)
  .addConfigPage({ title: 'Configuration', icon: 'cog', body: AppConfig, id: 'configuration' });

docs.title: 6. Docs
docs.text: Add a page under docs/plugins/<name>/ and wire it into mkdocs.yml nav. The PR lane runs mkdocs build --strict, so broken nav/links fail the build.

docs.title: Choosing panel vs app
docs.text: You want to… Use a… Add a visualization to dashboards, driven by datasource queries Panel plugin Add a custom page / whole experience with its own navigation App plugin

docs.title: AIgent Squad Chat
docs.text:
• Plugin ID: staffops-aigent-squad-chat-app
  • Type: app
  • Package: packages/staffops-aigent-squad-chat-app

A Grafana app plugin that provides a conversational UI to AIgent Squad — an external SRE-agentic system (OpenAI-compatible API, specialist subagents). The plugin is a thin chat client: it streams the conversation and renders it; AIgent Squad owns all orchestration and tool execution (Grafana / Loki / Tempo / PromQL / Kubernetes) server-side.

graph LR
    U[User] --> UI["Chat page (React)"]
    UI -->|"grafana/llm"| LLM["Grafana LLM app"]
    LLM -->|"OpenAI chat/completions"| SQUAD["AIgent Squad"]
    SQUAD --> TOOLS[("Loki / Tempo / PromQL / K8s")]

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description Streaming chat Tokens render as they arrive over Grafana Live. Thinking indicator "AIgent Squad is working…" while a tool runs server-side. Multi-turn Full conversation history is replayed each turn. Reasoning panel The <think> tool-trace is parsed into a collapsed panel, separate from the answer. See Reasoning & Trace. Stop / retry Cancel an in-flight stream or re-run after an error, preserving partial content. Availability gate Degrades gracefully when the Grafana LLM app is missing/unconfigured. Configuration page Model, source tag, timeouts, reasoning default — no secrets. See Configuration.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Grafana 13.x (declared grafanaDependency >= 12.3.0).
  • The Grafana LLM app (grafana-llm-app) installed and enabled, with a provider configured to the AIgent Squad endpoint. It is a declared plugin dependency.
  • Access restricted to Editor role and above.

docs.title: Architecture (Option A)
docs.text: The provider URL + token live in the Grafana LLM app (secureJsonData); the browser never sees them. See Architecture for the full rationale (Option A vs a self-contained Go backend) and the guardrail-compatibility decision.

docs.title: Option A: thin client behind the Grafana LLM app
docs.text:
Browser (this plugin, React)                 — no secret, no endpoint in the browser
  │  @grafana/llm streamChatCompletions()      (streams over Grafana Live)
  ▼
Grafana LLM app (grafana-llm-app)             — holds the AIgent Squad URL + token
  │  OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions
  ▼
AIgent Squad (external)                       — subagents + tools (Loki/Tempo/PromQL/K8s)

AIgent Squad is registered as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider inside the Grafana LLM app (provider type openai with a custom url). The plugin never sees the endpoint or token — they live in the LLM app's secureJsonData.

docs.title: Why Option A (vs a Go backend)
docs.text:
Option A — LLM app Option B — Go backend in the plugin Secret handling LLM app holds it server-side Plugin backend holds it New moving parts Reuses an installed app Adds a Go backend to a frontend-only repo Streaming @grafana/llm over Grafana Live Custom SSE passthrough Chosen ✅ Fallback only

Option A was validated end-to-end (Grafana 13.0.2 + grafana-llm-app v1.0.8): Bearer auth forwarded, streaming works over Grafana Live, and long tool-call pauses survive without timeout.

docs.title: Provider URL gotcha
docs.text: grafana-llm-app appends /v1/ to the configured base URL. Configure the provider URL without the /v1 suffix (e.g. https://aigent-squad.<domain>), otherwise requests hit /v1/v1/chat/completions and 404.

docs.title: Guardrail compatibility — no system message
docs.text:
AIgent Squad's Bedrock guardrail treats an injected system prompt as untrusted input and blocks it (HTTP 403). The plugin therefore sends no system message — the squad has its own system prompt. Instead, the latest user turn is prefixed with a configurable source tag ([source:grafana-plugin/aigent-squad-chat]) for audit/filtering on the squad side.

Root fix on the squad side

The squad also strips system messages before the guardrail (so any OpenAI client — LibreChat, Continue.dev — works). The plugin's no-system-message behavior is the client-side half of that contract.

docs.title: Streaming behavior
docs.text:
AIgent Squad pseudo-streams: it runs to completion (executing tools), then emits the answer as a burst of SSE chunks. During the wait the UI shows the thinking indicator; when the burst arrives, @grafana/llm's accumulateContent() renders it progressively. True token-by-token streaming is deferred to a future squad release.

Frontend safety timers:

Timer Default Purpose Thinking-idle 3s Switch to the "working…" indicator when no chunk arrives. Max stream idle 120s Hard error if no chunk of any kind arrives (tool runs can be long).

Both are adjustable on the Configuration page.

docs.title: AIgent Squad Chat — Configuration
docs.text:
There are two places to configure, with a clean separation of concerns:

  1. Provider (secret) → the Grafana LLM app. URL + token, never in this plugin.
  2. Behaviour knobs → this plugin's Configuration page. No secrets.

docs.title: 1. Provider — in the Grafana LLM app
docs.text:
Configure AIgent Squad as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider in the LLM app settings (secureJsonData), or via provisioning:

apiVersion: 1
apps:
  - type: grafana-llm-app
    org_id: 1
    disabled: false
    jsonData:
      openAI:
        provider: openai
        url: https://aigent-squad.<domain>   # NO /v1 suffix — the app appends it
    secureJsonData:
      openAIKey: $__env{AIGENT_SQUAD_TOKEN}

  - type: staffops-aigent-squad-chat-app
    org_id: 1
    disabled: false

docs.title: 2. Plugin behaviour — Configuration page
docs.text:
Administration → Plugins → AIgent Squad Chat → Configuration. Persisted in the plugin's jsonData (no secrets):

Setting Default Purpose Model base Model slot requested from the LLM app (the squad routes by context). Source tag [source:grafana-plugin/aigent-squad-chat] Prefix on the latest user message for audit/filtering. Empty disables it. Thinking indicator delay (ms) 3000 Idle time before the "working…" indicator. Max stream idle (ms) 120000 Hard timeout if no chunk arrives. Expand tool trace by default off Whether the reasoning panel starts expanded.

Defaults live in src/config.ts, so the plugin works with no configuration.

docs.title: Local end-to-end stack
docs.text:
The package ships a docker-compose.e2e.yaml (Grafana 13.x + grafana-llm-app + the built plugin) plus provisioning. Provide the token via env:

export AIGENT_SQUAD_TOKEN=<token>     # e.g. from your secret store
docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yaml up -d
# open http://localhost:3000 → AIgent Squad Chat

docs.title: AIgent Squad Chat — Reasoning & Trace
docs.text:
AIgent Squad wraps its tool-trace / reasoning in a <think>…</think> block (the reasoning-model convention) and emits the final answer after the closing tag:

<think>
🧭 Routed to observability (confidence 95%)
🔧 query(query='histogram_quantile(0.95, …)', tenant='0')
📦 ok
…
</think>
The p95 latency for DataPlatform.People in prd is …

Rendering that verbatim would dump the whole trace into the answer bubble. The plugin (src/llm/reasoning.ts) splits and structures it instead.

docs.title: splitReasoning
docs.text:
Separates the <think> block from the answer. Handles:

  • No block → the whole content is the answer (backward-compatible).
  • Open block (streaming) → everything after <think> is reasoning-in-progress; the answer is empty until </think> arrives.
  • Closed block → reasoning is the inner text; the answer is everything outside.

docs.title: parseTrace
docs.text:
Turns the raw trace into a compact structure:

  • Routing — 🧭 Routed to <specialist> (confidence N%).
  • Tool calls — one clean tool → result entry each; the verbose query args are dropped.
  • Summary — a one-line header, e.g. observability (95%) · 2× metrics · 25× query.

docs.title: Robustness — nothing is dropped
docs.text: Any trace line that is not a recognized tool / result / route pattern is preserved as a note entry rather than silently discarded. If the squad starts emitting free-text reasoning or a new trace format, it still surfaces in the panel — no plugin change needed. Only the fixed 🔧 Tool trace header is dropped as noise.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
• The answer renders as sanitized markdown (renderMarkdown — marked + XSS sanitizer).
  • The trace renders in a collapsed-by-default <details> panel (scrollable, monospace). The Expand tool trace by default setting controls the initial state.
  • Markdown containment: code blocks, tables and lists are constrained to the bubble (min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, list padding) so nothing bleeds outside.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: splitReasoning and parseTrace are covered by unit tests (src/llm/reasoning.test.ts) including the streaming (open-block), no-block, inline-result, aggregation, and note-preservation cases. Overall plugin coverage is ~99% lines.

docs.title: Service Map Panel
docs.text:
• Plugin ID: staffops-servicemap-panel
  • Type: panel
  • Package: packages/staffops-servicemap-panel

A directed service map (DAG) panel that renders service-to-service topology from Tempo service-graph metrics (a Prometheus-compatible source). It visualizes health, traffic, and dependencies, and lets you drill from an edge/node into Explore.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description DAG layout Services as nodes, calls as directed edges, laid out automatically. Health coloring Nodes/edges colored by error rate and latency thresholds. Animated traffic Particles flow along edges proportional to request rate. Cascade filtering Selecting a node isolates its upstream/downstream (multi-hop). Node kinds Distinct styling per node kind (service, database, queue, external). Zoom / pan Interactive navigation of large graphs. Drill-down Jump from a node/edge to Grafana Explore with the relevant query.

docs.title: Data source
docs.text: The panel consumes Tempo service-graph metrics exposed through a Prometheus-compatible datasource (e.g. traces_service_graph_request_total, traces_service_graph_request_failed_total, and the request/duration histograms). No Go backend — the panel transforms the DataFrames Grafana passes in.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The panel is distributed as a signed plugin zip (GitHub Releases). For a prod-like local test it can be installed at startup:

environment:
  - GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS=<release-zip-url>;staffops-servicemap-panel
  - GF_PLUGINS_ALLOW_LOADING_UNSIGNED_PLUGINS=staffops-servicemap-panel

See Configuration for panel options.

docs.title: Service Map Panel — Configuration
docs.text: The panel is configured like any Grafana panel: add it to a dashboard, point it at a datasource that exposes Tempo service-graph metrics, and adjust the panel options.

docs.title: Data requirements
docs.text:
The panel expects service-graph series (Prometheus-compatible). Typical queries:

# Request rate per edge (client → server)
sum by (client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total[$__rate_interval]))

# Error rate per edge
sum by (client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_failed_total[$__rate_interval]))

# Latency (p99) per edge
histogram_quantile(0.99,
  sum by (client, server, le) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_server_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))

The transform layer pairs client/server labels into edges and aggregates the metrics into node/edge health.

docs.title: Panel options
docs.text: Option Effect Health thresholds Error-rate / latency cutoffs that drive node & edge coloring. Traffic animation Toggle animated particles; density scales with request rate. Node kind mapping Map label values to node kinds (service / database / queue / external) for styling. Cascade / isolation Enable click-to-isolate upstream/downstream (multi-hop) filtering. Drill-down target The Explore datasource/query template opened when drilling from a node/edge.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
cd packages/staffops-servicemap-panel
cp .env.example .env      # set METRICS_URL and TEMPO_URL
# build + run a local Grafana with the panel (via Docker)

See Building & Testing for the Docker build commands.
